title: Ramp & Replay Ensemble for Dedicated Capacity Certification
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement a ramp-and-replay ensemble harness to certify Dedicated capacity SLAs with realistic tenant mixes, burst patterns, and autoscaler interactions. This ticket covers the benchmark blueprint, infra provisioning for isolated replay lanes, standardized load profiles, and an operator-facing customer acceptance checklist for onboarding Dedicated customers. Goal: provide reproducible verification runs that map workload characteristics to guaranteed throughput and sustainable tail latency under our autoscaling policies.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A harness that can replay recorded production traffic with configurable tenant weighting and sequence-length distributions.
2) Automated ramp schedules (warmup, ramp, sustain, cool-down) and bursts that exercise autoscaler thresholds.
3) Baseline runs that produce stable throughput/L95/L99 metrics for three canonical profiles: conversational short (<=64 tokens), assistant long (>=512 tokens), embedding-only.
4) A customer-facing acceptance checklist that maps run outputs to pass/fail (throughput headroom > 15%, sustained L99 < 500ms on dedicated tier SLOs, no error-rate regressions).
5) Run artifacts (raw traces, token-level cost, autoscaler events) are stored in a reproducible artifact bundle and surfaced in console QA dashboard.
implementation_notes:
- Reuse the existing replay driver but extend with an orchestrator that composes multiple replay lanes to emulate noisy neighbors.
- Add a tenant-awareness layer to inject per-tenant quotas and priority classes.
- Instrument autoscaler hooks: emit synthetic load when activating/deactivating nodes to capture transition tail effects.
- Work with infra to provision ephemeral isolated fleets (dedicated test pools) to avoid perturbing production.
- Provide a simple YAML profile format (ramp, tenant_mix, seq_len_dist, burst_schedule) for customers and solutions engineers.
test_plan:
- Phase A (dev smoke): small-scale replay against a canary dedicated pool to validate correctness of tenant weighting and sequencing.
- Phase B (stability): full-scale run for each canonical profile for 2 hours sustained to capture steady-state.
- Phase C (stress & failovers): introduce node failures and region fallback to validate graceful degradation and throughput guarantees.
- Phase D (customer acceptance): run the harness using a customer's sanitized production trace with the customer present; produce acceptance report and signoff artifact.
runbook:
1) Checkout harness repo and select profile YAML.
2) Provision ephemeral test pool: apply Terraform module redwood/test-dedicated-pool with tags.
3) Start telemetry capture (traces, per-node CPU/GPU, autoscaler events).
4) Execute ramp-replay; monitor console dashboard and slack alert channel.
5) After run, upload artifact bundle to GCS and trigger report generator.
6) Notify PM/SE for customer review and signoff.
metrics:
- Throughput (reqs/sec, tokens/sec)
- Tail latencies (P95, P99, P99.9)
- Error rates (HTTP 5xx, model timeouts)
- Autoscaler actions (scale up/down events, cooldown durations)
- Cost per 1M tokens during run
- Headroom percentage vs committed throughput
risk_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Replaying sanitized customer traces may leak sensitive tokens. Mitigation: apply token scrubbing pipeline and run within VPC with KMS-backed keys.
- Risk: Test pools accidentally consume capacity needed for production. Mitigation: strong tagging and quota guardrails; run during maintenance windows or on isolated org projects.
- Risk: Autoscaler flapping during synthetic bursts leads to non-deterministic results. Mitigation: standardize burst patterns and include stabilization windows in profiles.
